Reading all the files I need to understand before touching anything. Now read App.tsx and theme.ts to understand the current theme state, and CommitFlow to understand the buyer-side order panel: Now I have full visibility. Also read the theme file: Now I have everything. Let me set up the todo list and work through all four items systematically. **Step 0: sync workspace — delete home/, TierCurveEditor, strip SupplierView, revert theme to two-state.** Strip the TierCurveEditor import and usage block from SupplierView: Now restore the two-state theme toggle in App.tsx. Replace the three-way pill with a simple sun/moon icon button: Step 0 done. Now **Step 1: smart tokensPerUnit auto-suggest + per-token price input on sell page + buyer-side token display.**

The key logic for auto-suggest: when a token with a market rate is selected, compute the largest "round amount" from a candidate list whose value at market rate is ≤ $5. For EURC/GBPA (≈$1) that's 1; for MXNB (≈$0.053) that's 50 (50 × $0.053 ≈ $2.65); for WETH (≈$2200) that's 0.001; for cirBTC (≈$70k) that's 0.00001.

The tier price inputs will show "Price per TOKEN" (not per unit) when `tokensPerUnit ≠ 1 whole token`. The value the seller enters is per-token; we convert to per-unit for the contract. The stock/min/max fields also flip to token amounts.

This is a significant change to SupplierView. I'll do it in targeted edits rather than a full rewrite: Add the `suggestTokensPerUnit` helper and integrate it. I'll add it after the existing helpers in SupplierView, then wire the auto-suggest and the per-token price input mode: Now wire the auto-suggest: when the token changes, if the seller has not manually edited `tokensPerUnitStr`, update it. Add a `tpuEdited` ref to track manual edits: Now add an effect that auto-suggests `tokensPerUnit` when the token or market rate changes (but not when the seller has manually edited): Now mark `tpuEditedRef` when the seller edits the field, and also reset it when they change token: Now mark the ref when the seller types in the tokensPerUnit input: Now add the "per-token price input" mode. When `tokensPerUnit ≠ 1 whole token` (i.e. `tokensPerUnit !== 10n ** BigInt(decimals)`), the tier price inputs are labeled "Price per TOKEN" and the value is per-token, with a note showing the per-unit equivalent. The validation must convert per-token → per-unit before checking the $5 cap.

First, add a computed boolean `isMultiUnit` and a helper to convert per-token price string to per-unit price string: Now update `parsedTiers` to use `perTokenToPerUnit` when in multi-unit mode: Update `validate()` to use `perTokenToPerUnit` in multi-unit mode. The validation function receives the raw `TierInput[]` strings. I need to pass `isMultiUnit` and `tokensPerUnit`/`decimals` into it, or do the conversion before passing. The cleanest approach: in the `validate` call, convert tier prices to per-unit strings first when in multi-unit mode: Also update `handlePost` to use `tiersForValidation`: Add `tiersForValidation` to the `handleApprove` and `handlePost` `useCallback` dep arrays: Now update the tier price input label and show per-unit equivalent when in multi-unit mode. Also update the `marketPricePerUnit` calculation for multi-unit mode (it should return per-token price): Now update the tier builder UI: change the price column label to "Price per TOKEN" in multi-unit mode and show the per-unit conversion beneath each price input. Also update the "$5 cap exceeded" error message: Now update the per-tier row to show per-unit equivalent when in multi-unit mode, and update the `$5 cap` message. First let me look at what the tier price derivation looks like in the render loop: Now update the validation error for the $5 cap to give a helpful message in multi-unit mode: Now for the **buyer side** (CommitFlow / OrderPreviewCard): when `tokensPerUnit ≠ oneWholeToken`, show quantity in tokens. The `OrderPreviewCard` already shows `tokensReceived` — I need to make the quantity picker label say tokens and update the "available" text. I'll add a prop `tokenDisplayMode` and update the label:

The spec says: "quantity is entered and shown in tokens ('0.1 WETH'), with the unit count small underneath ('100 units'); Max, +/- step by one unit." The picker already steps by 1 unit and the text field is in units. Rather than restructure the input, I'll show the token equivalent prominently and add a subtitle showing unit count. The quantity label changes to show "X WETH" equivalent.

This is a display change in `OrderPreviewCard`. I'll update it to show "Quantity in tokens" when `isMultiUnit`: `BigInt(10 ** goodsDecimals)` can overflow for decimals > 15. Use a safer comparison. Let me fix that: Good. Now **Step 2: centred calm homepage**. Delete the old `HomePage.tsx` and write a new clean one in place: Now App.tsx passes `onProof` and `onSelectDeal` to `HomePage`. The new `HomePage` only needs `onBrowse` and `onSell`. Update the call site: Now add the CSS variable `--hero-bg` for light theme. Check the existing CSS to find the right place: Add `--hero-bg` to both theme blocks. For light: soft pale-blue gradient. For dark: the deep dark-blue already hardcoded in the component (but the CSS variable lets us override): Also update the hero's light-theme text and radial glow to match the pale-blue hero background — the white text on `#e8f0f8` would be unreadable. The hero text color needs to be dark in light mode. Use `--ink` for headline and text in light mode via CSS variable override, or handle in the component by checking theme. The simplest approach: make the hero section adapt based on the theme. I'll use the `useTheme` hook in HomePage: Now wire those palette variables into the hero JSX: Now **Step 3: DealRoom — full-width header, single right card with dividers, equal gaps.** The DealRoom changes: move title/token/unit line to a full-width header row above the two columns; wrap CommitFlow + share + settle/claim + secondary buttons (gas toggle, add-network) all inside one card; equal `gap-5` on both columns. I'll also move the `handleAddNetwork` button from CommitFlow's bottom into DealRoom's right card footer, and consolidate the share row.

The key structural change is in `DealRoom.tsx`. CommitFlow ends with a standalone "Add Arc to wallet" button — I need to move that into the DealRoom right card. To do this cleanly, I'll extract it from CommitFlow into a prop `onAddNetwork`, or just duplicate the small button in DealRoom. The simplest change: remove the button from CommitFlow and add it alongside the gas-toggle link in the right card wrapper.

First, remove the standalone `handleAddNetwork` button from CommitFlow: Now update DealRoom to use the new layout — full-width header, equal gaps, and single right card: Now restructure the DealRoom render: full-width header above columns, unified right card, equal gaps: Now remove the `leftCol`'s title/token block since it's now in the full-width header, and remove the old separate `rightCol` (CommitFlow/share/settle/claim) since it's now in `rightCard`: Now remove the old `rightCol` variable (it's been replaced by `rightCard`): Also update `leftCol`'s gap to match the new `gap-5` between columns: Now run the check: Two issues: 1) The `(selectedToken` type assertion is missing a closing paren on the right type. 2) `handleAddNetwork` in `CommitFlow` is now unused (it was moved to `AddNetworkButton`). Fix both: The edit got mangled — `(selectedToken` is an unclosed expression. Fix it: Now remove the old `handleAddNetwork` from CommitFlow (the logic is now in `AddNetworkButton`): ```

tsc --noEmit: exit 0
``` Here is a precise account of every change.

**Step 0 (sync):** Deleted `src/swarm/home/` (all seven files from Turn 17b) and `src/swarm/TierCurveEditor.tsx`. Removed the `TierCurveEditor` import and usage block from `SupplierView.tsx`. Replaced the three-way theme pill in `App.tsx` with a single sun/moon icon button using `useTheme` + `toggleTheme` (the two-state API that was always in `theme.ts`).

**Step 1 (high-value token units):**
- `suggestTokensPerUnit(decimals, usdPerToken)` scans a fixed candidate list `[1, 0.5, 0.1, 0.05, …]` and returns the largest amount whose market value is at most $5 and whose decimal places fit the token. EURC/GBPA ($1) stay at `1`; MXNB (~$0.053) suggests `50`; WETH (~$2200) suggests `0.001`; cirBTC (~$70k) suggests `0.00001`.
- A `tpuEditedRef` tracks whether the seller has manually changed the field. An effect runs on token/rate change and writes the suggestion only when the ref is false. Selecting a new token resets the ref.
- `isMultiUnit` is true when `tokensPerUnit ≠ 10^decimals` (not exactly one whole token). When true: tier price inputs are labelled "Price per TOKEN (USDC)"; the entered value is per-token; `perTokenToPerUnit()` converts to per-unit for validation and chart; the per-unit equivalent is shown in small text under each input. `marketPricePerUnit` in multi-unit mode returns the per-token market price directly.
- Validation error for the $5 cap now says: "One unit would cost more than $5. Use a smaller unit, for example 0.001 WETH."
- `OrderPreviewCard` (buyer side): when `tokensPerUnit ≠ 10^decimals`, shows the token amount prominently above the unit picker with the unit count in small text alongside.

**Step 2 (homepage):** `HomePage.tsx` fully rewritten as a calm, centred three-section page. Hero: `--hero-bg` gradient (deep blue in dark mode, soft pale-blue in light) with a radial glow; centred headline and subtitle; a frosted search card with a text input and "Browse deals" button; token chips for each `GOODS_TOKENS` entry; "or sell on Swarm" text link. All hero colours (text, glow, chips, pill, icon) are computed from `useTheme()` so both modes look intentional. Stats band unchanged. "How it works" is three cards inside one large rounded container with a footer row containing the two CTAs. `--hero-bg` added to both theme blocks in `index.css`.

**Step 3 (deal room):** Title/description/token line moved to a full-width header block above the two columns, so both columns' first cards start at the same top edge. Right column is now one rounded card (`rightCard`): CommitFlow inside a `p-4` area, then a thin-divider row with `AddNetworkButton`, then an optional share footer row. Settle/refund and claim panels still appear above `rightCard` when relevant. The old separate share button and `rightCol` variable are gone. Column gap changed to `lg:gap-5` (consistent with `space-y-5` in the left column). `handleAddNetwork` moved to an exported `AddNetworkButton` component so CommitFlow no longer renders it.
